news.title: OCC Bans Direct Stablecoin Yield While Leaving Third-Party Rewards Under Review
news.body: The OCC finalized its GENIUS Act implementing rule on October 21, with an effective date of January 18, 2027. The rule prohibits issuers from paying direct yield to stablecoin holders and subjects third-party rewards to case-by-case review, giving distributors no blanket clearance for yield-like offers. The effective date does not itself authorize prospective issuers to launch: application timing and separate financial-crime rulemaking remain outstanding.

news.title: Cross River Targets Merchant Wallets and Loyalty With Planned Accrue Acquisition
news.body: Cross River’s parent agreed to acquire Accrue, whose branded wallets combine stored value, payments, rewards and customer engagement. The acquisition would add merchant-facing wallet technology to Cross River’s accounts, cards, payments and lending capabilities. The companies have not disclosed a purchase price or closing date, and the announcement does not establish merchant migration plans or processing-cost savings.

news.title: Relay and Nium Report Over $500 Million in First-Year Cross-Border Payment Volume
news.body: More than 500 Relay customers sent over $500 million to 153 countries during the first year of its Nium partnership, the companies reported. The figures measure usage of international payments embedded in Relay’s business-banking platform, not growth against an earlier period. Relay and Nium plan to expand the partnership but have not disclosed a quantified expansion target, payments margins or comparative FX pricing.

news.title: UK Proposes Lower iPhone Contactless Access Costs for Rival Payment Wallets
news.body: The UK competition watchdog is consulting on proposals to lower fees and remove technical barriers for competing payment providers accessing iPhone contactless technology. The measures would reduce access barriers for rival wallets, but the consultation does not itself implement new access terms. Final eligibility requirements, fees and implementation dates will determine the terms available to card issuers and wallet providers.

news.title: Global Fintech Funding Falls to $10.6 Billion, Down 28.4% From Q2
news.body: Fintech startups raised $10.6 billion globally in Q3 2026, Crunchbase reports, compared with $14.9 billion in Q2 and $13.5 billion a year earlier. Those totals represent declines of 28.4% quarter over quarter and 21.4% year over year. The aggregate decline does not establish financial distress at individual fintech suppliers or uniform deterioration across regions, funding stages and subsectors.

perspective: Relay–Nium payment volumes accompany merchant-wallet acquisitions, stablecoin rulemaking, UK contactless access proposals and lower fintech funding.
